records.statement: Reward-associated attentional capture is supported, but the traditional VDAC paradigm shows weak experimental effects and multiple methodological concerns.
records.reasoning_rule: Do not infer a large or universal reward-to-attention effect.

records.statement: Influencer trust-related effect sizes vary strongly across platform, geography, product and influencer type; some relationships show small-study/publication-bias signals.
records.reasoning_rule: Use context-specific interpretation and do not copy pooled r values into causal edge weights.

records.statement: Parasocial engagement correlates with outcomes, but not every connection-to-return or connection-to-sharing pathway is established as causal.
records.reasoning_rule: Keep these paths discounted or emerging until direct causal evidence is available.

records.statement: Repeated viewing or returning is not itself evidence of habit; habit requires context-linked repetition/automaticity and can coexist with goal-directed behavior.
records.reasoning_rule: Never label an audience as habitual from return-rate data alone.

records.statement: Identity-based influence depends on identification strength and social context; it is not generic conformity.
records.reasoning_rule: Require identity salience/context before making strong identity-based predictions.
